DIAGNOSIS from iter-1 SLURM log (765196): training CONVERGED by epoch 3 (loss 5.2e-6 ep3 -> 1.6e-6 ep7, asymptotically flat; wall tripped at ep7/14 in 1000s), and the VN settled at SSIM 0.805 BELOW its own FBP init (baseline SSIM ~0.84, baseline_PSNR 34.08). This is a CONVERGED-BUT-BAD basin, NOT under-training -- so epochs-up is INERT here (the proven epochs lever applied to genuinely under-trained trainers; this one has flat loss). lambda_t never moved from init (0.0023 across all 5 steps), so the tiny-DC + 16-filter regulariser converged to a BLUNT SMOOTHER that degrades the FBP init below baseline. SIX-BOX (NUMBERS): (1) iter-1 = SSIM 0.4554 / hr 0.000 (val_psnr 21.24, val_rmse 0.00434) in elapsed_s=170.2 -- only ~14% of the 1200s (20-min) train+score budget used; pretrain_epochs=12. (2) FAILURE MODE: the pretrain-denoiser-then-data-consistency path UNDER-CONVERGES in the budget (same as v1, which was stuck at 0.441). The k=3 DC steps refine a denoiser that has not yet learned the Mayo image statistics; SSIM 0.455 is far below the end-to-end itnet_v3 sibling (0.896). With only 12 pretrain epochs at lr=1e-4 the denoiser is under-trained, and 170s/1200s proves the budget was almost entirely idle. (3) ONE KNOB: pretrain_epochs 12->48, mirroring the SIBLING itnet (v1) iter-2 which raised pretrain_epochs 8->48 and jumped SSIM 0.441->0.593 (+0.15) under THIS campaign and metric -- the strongest just-proven signal that pretraining was the v1/v2 bottleneck. Chosen over lr-up (v3 is unstable above 1e-4; mirror the safe v1 move) and over architecture knobs (k/unet_c) which would change the model not the convergence. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if pretrain_epochs 12->48, val_ssim rises substantially above 0.4554 (toward v1 iter-2's ~0.59, possibly the ~0.88-0.90 sibling band) because more pretraining lets the denoiser converge before the k=3 DC refinement, exactly as it did for v1. FALSIFIER: if val_ssim stays flat (<=~0.47) at 48 epochs, the pretrain-DC architecture is CAPPED in this budget regardless of pretraining (not an under-training problem), and iter-3 must move toward end-to-end unrolled training (the v3 recipe) or accept the pretrain-DC path is budget-limited. (5) BUDGET: HARD 20-min train+score. iter-1 ran 12 epochs + 214-slice per-sample val + figure in 170s; the per-epoch pretrain cost over 200 stratified slices is the variable part and the 214-slice per-sample val + figure are roughly fixed. 4x the epochs is roughly 4x the small pretrain base plus the single fixed val/figure pass: est well under 600s, far below 1200s; max_train_s=960 is a 16-min HARD backstop so train always leaves room for the 214-slice per-sample val + figure inside the 30-min sbatch wall. val_n=214 KEPT (NOT reduced), grad_clip=1.0 KEPT. ONE KNOB: epochs 8->24 (3x). All else identical to iter-1 (proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=3 -> 12 trainable params unchanged; 3*(proj_n_bf+img_n_bf)). SIX-BOX: (1) iter-1 = SSIM 0.919 / hr 0.0279 in elapsed 254s -- only ~21% of the 1200s (20-min) budget used; 12-param bilateral, lr=5e-3. (2) FAILURE MODE: high SSIM but near-zero hr because the calibrated RMSE-sensitive headroom metric does not credit the bilateral's smoothing (campaign note: SSIM rewards the BF blur, headroom does not). Critically, with only 12 params at lr=5e-3 and 8 epochs the supervised-MSE loss -- which IS RMSE-sensitive, unlike SSIM -- has had little chance to drive the scalar sigmas to their RMSE-optimal (less-smoothing) values: the run is UNDER-TRAINED (254s/1200s). (3) ONE KNOB: epochs 8->24. JUSTIFICATION vs the other candidate (img_n_bf up): adding image-domain bilateral DEPTH at the current loose img_sr=0.02 would smooth MORE, which keeps SSIM high but does NOT lift the RMSE-driven hr (more blur is the wrong direction for headroom); whereas more epochs lets the MSE objective itself pull the sigmas toward the RMSE optimum AND uses the idle ~950s budget. epochs is the cleaner lever for the hr deficit. (4) HYPOTHESIS: if epochs 8->24, then hr rises above 0.0279 (toward the dual_domain_supervised U-Net sibling's 0.276) because the 12 BF sigmas are under-trained at 8 epochs and the supervised-MSE gradient -- being RMSE-sensitive -- will sharpen them. FALSIFIER: if hr stays <=~0.03 (flat) at 24 epochs, the 12-param bilateral is at its CAPACITY ceiling on the 2304-view Mayo FBP (not an under-training problem), and iter-3 must instead add capacity (img_n_bf up) or attack the proj-domain over-smoothing (proj_sr) -- epochs is then exhausted. (5) BUDGET: HARD 20-min train+score. iter-1 ran 8 epochs + 214-slice per-sample val + figure in 254s; per-step cost is dominated by the SHARED 2304-view FBP adjoint, not the 12 BF params, so 24 epochs ~= 3x train ~= 8 epochs*3 plus the single fixed val pass: est ~600-760s << 1200s. Comfortably inside the 30-min sbatch wall. val_n=214 KEPT (NOT reduced), grad_clip=1.0 KEPT. (6) Loop continues -- no control returned. rationale: hammernik_vn-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, vn_init=fbp, vn_dc_norm=True, vn_checkpoint=True, vn_normalize_filters=False, epochs=14, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=FRESH search-20260619-01 iter-1 FEASIBILITY (corrected protocol: val=ALL 214 L277 slices + 321px detector-geometry FOV; HARD 20-min train+score budget; staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP init + per-step model.projector swap, bg_target=truth, no fov= override). Hammernik-VN = MRI variational net ported to CT: T untied unrolled steps, each = learned filter-bank + per-filter RBF activation (the _rho_prime bump loop) PLUS an in-loop PYRO-NN projector data-consistency step (architectural twin of LPD/ItNet but tiny interpretable regulariser). CRITICAL LESSON from the SIBLING hammernik_2017 iter-1: it did NOT diverge to 0.0 -- it CUDA-OOM'd in _rho_prime at 72s with batch_size=4 (16GB RTX5000; the (B,F,H,W)=(4,16,512,512) x 31-bump RBF tensors + 5-step autograd blew the card). So the dominant iter-1 risk here is MEMORY, not divergence. MITIGATION: batch_size=2 (NOT 4), vn_n_filters=16 (below the 24 default -> fewer RBF tensors), vn_checkpoint=true (gradient-checkpoints each unrolled step -- hammernik_vn HAS this knob, cuts activation memory ~T-fold; this is the key difference that lets the projector-in-loop VN fit where the 2017 batch=4 did not). STABILITY against the documented VN family divergence/NaN->0.0 trap: grad_clip=1.0 (MANDATORY -- the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward; clip_and_step also SKIPS nonfinite-gradient batches so a poisoned step can't collapse the recon to a constant), vn_dc_norm=true (power-iter normalizes R^T(Rx-g) so softplus(lambda_t) stays O(1) regardless of geometry -- the safeguard the projector-less 2017 lacked), lr=5e-4 (the documented hammernik_vn optimum from the discarded run; 8e-4 was worse, brief caps lr<=5e-4), vn_lambda_init=2.3e-3 (loose VN-port working-corner hint). CAPACITY conservative per brief: vn_T=5, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0 (FBP recon is ~O(1) so the RBF grid [-1,1] covers it). BUDGET: reference -- LPD (projector-in-loop, T=7, ep30, train200, score214) ran 1150s/19.2min right at the edge; hammernik_vn at T=5/N_k=16/checkpointed should be comparable-or-cheaper per step. max_train_s=1000 (16.7min in-solver wall) is the BINDING constraint (epochs=14 is just an upper bound the wall trips first), leaving ~3min for score(214)+figure under the 30min SLURM kill.
